The transitional design plan provides an integrated approach to transition planning. It improves alignment of service management cutover and deployment plans, and helps to:

  • Plan appropriate capacity and resources for transitional states, and process flows including all necessary work-arounds and temporary interfaces.
  • Provide support for the service transition teams and people.
  • Plan the changes required in a manner that maintains the integrity of all identified customer assets, service assets and configurations as they evolve through service transition.
  • Verify that service transition issues, risks and deviations are reported to the appropriate stakeholders and decision makers.
    Coordinate activities across projects, suppliers and service teams where required.
  • Periodically update the transitional design plan to account for changes that affect cutover planning, to verify that the plan is up-to-date and reflects the latest state of the implementation.

Transition design planning should address:

  • Planning and coordination of resources so that the requirements in the service management strategy and plan are effectively realized.
  • Identification, management and control the risks of failure and disruption across transition activities.
  • Assurance that all parties adopt the common framework of standard re-usable processes and supporting systems.
  • Provision of clear and comprehensive plans that enable the customer and business change projects to align their activities with the service management plan.
  • Management of all necessary work-arounds and temporary interfaces.

The transitional design plan is a living document until the final version is signed off. New inputs, constraints and business requirements will drive periodic updates to the transitional design plan.

To improve a service management team's ability to handle change and to define steps that manage transition from the current state to the future state organization, processes, and information technology solution.

Periodically review and update the transitional design plan

To enable more current and complete assessments of scope change impacts, timing, and dependencies impacting the cutover, review the baseline cutover and deployment transition design plan at agreed intervals.  Determine potential impacts and potential risks to the cutover window, make changes as necessary, and communicate the most up-to-date information to inform re-planning to key stakeholders. 

  • Review the baseline version of the cutover and deployment plan with impacted project teams and business stakeholders during the middle-to-later-part of the build activity
  • Determine changes to key business and technical activities along with their readiness criteria and approach (e.g., new or modified old tasks, dependencies and durations and impacts due to new change requests)
  • Seek PMO input on the overall progress of the implementation plan to identify dependencies and potential impacts to the cutover plan
  • Seek inputs from program leadership for additional considerations (e.g., overall change in direction, release plan, deployment options) in order to identify potential impacts to the cutover plan
  • Incorporate all applicable changes into the revised version of the cutover and deployment plan
    • Update the plan for resource planning and coordination
    • Update controls to address potential disruptions across transition activities
    • Update the framework of standard re-usable processes and supporting systems
    • Make adjustments to provide work-arounds for critical business processes in case of failures
    • Add or make changes to temporary interfaces required during transition as a result of detailed cutover activities information.
  • Review significant impacts to the cutover window and timing with program leadership, especially if go-live date changes are possible
  • Distribute the updated plan to all workstream leads, PMO, program and business leadership
